reasoning_traces.think:
The core innovation lies in transforming multi-dimensional, spatiotemporal pressure data into a structured graph representation—specifically, the Player Pressure Map (PPM). Each player is modeled as a node in a graph where edges represent interaction dynamics. The pressure matrix for each player is derived from directional pitch control values, capturing the influence of defenders. These matrices are aggregated into a graph structure, enabling the application of Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) to predict possession risk. The GNN learns to associate high-pressure configurations with increased likelihood of losing possession. This dual approach of spatial quantification and graph-based modeling ensures that both local player dynamics and global team pressure are captured. Failure modes include data gaps in tracking or misalignment between visual and positional cues. The system assumes consistent player behavior patterns and stable game contexts, which may break down in unpredictable or chaotic game moments.
